title: AI driven facial animation for NPC dialogue
author: benawheeler
selftext:
Hey folks just wanted to share something I’ve been working on. Was never truly satisfied with the quality of NVIDIA’s audio2Face or unreal engines in engine animation models, so I decided to learn how to build my own.

This model takes an input of an audio clip and predicts the face rig that aligns with it. Trained on in the wild video.

It’s a little rough on lip sync still but it’s very possible to improve it. Also, in the video it’s inference on 5 second audio clips with a little gap so ignore where the Metahuman snaps back to a neutral position.

What do people think of the quality and how practical it would be to integrate into your workflows? Appreciate any thoughts.

comments.body: wow that's good. I used audio2face on a project with some indecisive writers and the quick turnaround was great - but this one here looks is genuinely impressive. What I'd require though would be a conversion to ARKit blendshapes, mainly for use with other software/rigs ( I don't use metahumans, they're usually too heavy or I need to create entirely different characters for specific applications etc.)

replies.author: Infinitecontextlabs
replies.body: Isn't it basically a matter of more points in the face rig trained on the same video?

replies.author: benawheeler
replies.body:
Right yeah the midface is actually what I care most about because it has the least signal coming from audio. 

Lipsync in theory is easier because it closely maps to audio with phonemes, but the mid face has a big one-to-many problem where there’s a lot of potential expressions the face could plausibly make given some audio. Like blinks, head movements, eye movements all that just isn’t that correlated with audio. 

This is why MSE regression sucks for the upper face because it just averages is out.

Yeah this is kind of the bar I’m going for. It’s very hard to get it better than real motion capture obviously. 

I was thinking jt could be used mostly for in game dialogue where realtime generation is really needed, even if it’s still a multiple choice style dialogue tree like Detroit becoming human, or just making it easier for smaller teams to add dialogue animation without needing a motion capture studio.
